gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Creative Pebble Pro and Pebble X Plus reach their headline 30 W RMS only on a separately sold 30 W USB PD adapter, and that this adapter port carries power only, with no USB audio. A PC user who wants full power is therefore on Bluetooth (SBC only) or AUX. On a PC's own USB-C port with USB audio they get 10 W RMS (Pebble Pro) or 15 W RMS (Pebble X Plus). The mains-powered Creative T60 gives 30 W RMS while taking USB-C audio.
standout_why: I checked against StackandValue (cited in chat 1). It already says the Pebble Pro gives up to 10 W RMS on a standard USB port and up to 30 W RMS with a 30 W PD adapter sold separately. By my reader's summary, it does not say the PD port gives up USB audio, does not give the Pebble X Plus split, and does not set either against the T60's 30 W RMS on mains power. Its other figures mix units: 40 W RMS / 80 W peak for the Logitech Z407, RMS only for the Edifier R1280DBs, and peak only for the Klipsch ProMedia 2.1. I could not read the other cited pages through the fetch tool: Tom's Hardware, TechRadar, Tom's Guide and PC Gamer returned only the page title, and Wired blocked the fetch. So I can't rule out that one of them has the full point. The idea that power depends on the adapter is partly covered. Losing USB audio in 30 W mode, the X Plus split, and the T60 comparison are what this page would add.
decides: It changes the pick for a shopper who wants wired USB audio from a PC, which is the setup both ChatGPT answers pushed for gaming and calls. In that setup the Pebble Pro ($66.49) gives 10 W RMS and the Pebble X Plus ($123.49) gives 15 W RMS. The T60 ($94.99, with its own 18 V 2 A adapter) gives 30 W RMS while playing USB-C audio. ChatGPT's 'best overall value' Pebble Pro is a third as loud as the T60 in the mode ChatGPT recommended, unless the shopper buys a 30 W PD brick and moves to Bluetooth SBC or AUX. The Pebble Pro is still the right pick for a small desk where 10 W RMS is enough. For more volume over USB, the T60 is the better buy, and it costs less than the X Plus.
